Attendance and participation at the City of La Verne Planning Commission meetings are welcomed and
appreciated. Community engagement provides the Planning Commission with valuable information. Regular
Meetings are held on the 2nd Wednesday of every month. In compliance with the American Disabilities Act, any
person with a disability who requires a modification or accommodation in order to participate in a meeting
should contact the City Clerk’s Office at (909) 596-8726 at least 48 hours prior to the meeting.

The Council Chambers will be open to the public at 6:00 p.m. Materials related to an item on this agenda,
submitted to the Planning Commission after distribution of the agenda packet, are available for public
inspection at the meeting or in the Community Development Department during normal business hours.

  Principal Planner Candice Bowcock presented her staff report. The
  applicant was not present at the meeting.

  Chairperson Simison opened the Public Hearing. There were no
  comments. Chairperson Simison closed the Public Hearing.

  The commissioners had concerns regarding the finality of the one-year
  extension, if more time is needed by the applicant.

  Ms. Bowcock stated that it can be extended again if needed. Mr. Kress

CITY OF LA VERNE
Community Development Department

DATE:  October 12, 2022

TO:  Planning Commission

FROM:  Nicholas Conti, Planning Intern

SUBJECT:  Case No. 108-22CUP – 1965 Foothill Blvd – A request to obtain a
  Conditional Use Permit for Tacos Don Cuco Type 41 On-Site Beer and
  Wine License.

AGENDA SUMMARY

The applicant, Jonathan Rios, is requesting approval for a Conditional Use Permit for a
Type 41 beer and wine license at 1965 Foothill Boulevard. Suites M and N. The
restaurant is located within the Foothill Boulevard Specific Plan, which requires approval
of a conditional use permit for the on-site sale of beer and wine.

RECOMMENDATION:

Staff and the Development Review Committee recommends approval to the Planning
Commission of Resolution No. 1298, approving Case No. 108-22CUP, based on the
findings and the proposed conditions of approval.

BACKGROUND:

Tacos Don Cuco will be located 1965 Foothill Boulevard Suites M & N, in the Foothill
Boulevard Specific Plan. Next Republic was previously located here in 2018 and
operated as a restaurant, and while they were able to serve beer and wine as the space
historically served alcohol, there was no Conditional Use Permit on file. Prior to Next
Republic, the space was occupied by a variety of restaurants. Most recently in 2020,
there was going to be an Okami Sushi restaurant at this location, however due to the
pandemic they were unable to open. Tacos Don Cuco is a franchise with many stores in
Texas and two stores in California. They focus on serving authentic tacos along with
breakfast, seafood and specialty dishes while only using high quality ingredients. The
Foothill Boulevard Specific Plan permits the on-site sale of beer, wine, and spirits in
conjunction with an eating establishment when a conditional use permit has been
granted. All restaurants with on-site sales of beer and wine must comply with State
Alcoholic Beverage Control regulations and the sale of alcohol must be incidental to that
of food service.
 PC Agenda Report
Case No. 108-22CUP
October 12, 2022
Page 2

The La Verne Municipal Code limits hours of operation for businesses to between 6:00
a.m. and midnight, and Tacos Don Cuco has indicated that their hours of operation
would be 10:00 a.m. – 10:00 p.m. Staff has included a condition of approval limiting the
hours for alcohol sales to 6:00 a.m. to midnight daily for the restaurant.

PROPOSAL:

On September 1st, 2022, the applicant, Jonathan Rios, submitted a Conditional Use
Permit application for a Type 41 license for the restaurant. A Type 41 license authorizes
the on-sale of beer and wine for consumption of the licensee’s business. Also, the Type
41 license allows for the sale of alcohol for consumption of the licensee’s premises. The
business must maintain suitable kitchen facilities and must make actual and substantial
sales of meals for consumption on the premises. There are no exterior or interior
modifications being proposed at this time. Tacos Don Cuco is expecting to have 4
employees and if need be, they will hire a 5th employee if there is a demand.

Floor Plan - The proposed business will be located east of the main shopping center
anchor tenant (Michaels). The proposed business will occupy a combined two thousand
twenty-nine (2,029) square foot tenant space, which will include a dining area, a kitchen,
two bathrooms, a walk-in cooler, a walk-in freezer, a service station, and an office.
Access to the business will be through two (2) front doors.

Parking - The proposed restaurant would require twenty-one (21) spaces based on the
parking ratio of one space per every one hundred square feet (1:100). This was
calculated based on the business being classified as a restaurant, which requires a
parking ratio of one per one hundred (1:100). The total number of spaces required for
the Emerald Center is three hundred and sixteen (316) spaces and there are three
hundred and forty-five (345) total confirmed spaces. In order to operate, the restaurant
would require twenty-one (21) parking spaces and since there is an excess of twenty-
nine (29) spaces, staff does not believe that the business will have a significant impact
on parking.

COMPATIBILITY WITH SURROUNDING USES:

Surrounding land uses include:

North: Mobile Home Park - Residential
South: Foothill Boulevard - Commercial
East: Mobile Home Park - Residential
West: Foothill Boulevard - Commercial
 PC Agenda Report
Case No. 108-22CUP
October 12, 2022
Page 3

Tacos Don Cuco will be located on Foothill Boulevard within the Big Lots and Michaels
Center and is within the Foothill Boulevard Specific Plan. The surrounding land uses
vary from restaurants and retail stores to residential. To the north and east of the
subject property is the Mobile Home Park; to the south and west is mix of restaurants
and stores within the existing shopping center. The proposed application for Tacos Don
Cuco beer and wine license should not impact the existing commercial and residential
uses found in the surrounding area.

ENVIRONMENTAL REVIEW:

This project is categorically exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act per
Section 15301(Class 1, Existing Facilities). No further environmental review is required.
